The toolkit

sf Vector

Simple Features

Reading GeoJSON and shapefiles, assigning and transforming coordinate systems, buffering, spatial joins and point-in-polygon counting.

Used in all five exercises
tm Cartography

tmap 4.x

Choropleths, classification methods, colour schemes, small multiples, raster layers and interactive maps, written against the v4 API.

Used in four exercises
sp Point patterns

spatstat

Kernel density estimation, bandwidth selection, the Clark-Evans test and the G, F, K and L summary functions with Monte Carlo envelopes.

Used in two exercises
tr Raster

terra

The raster data model: building grids, rasterising point layers, and converting density surfaces for cartographic output.

Used in two exercises
gg Statistics

ggstatsplot

Charts that carry their own confirmatory test, turning a visual impression into a reportable correlation with a confidence interval.

Used in one exercise
tv Wrangling

tidyverse

Import, reshape and join with readr, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2 and purrr throughout.

Used in all five exercises

Course progress

Lesson 1 · Geospatial data models and mapping

3 exercises

Vector and raster data models, geographic versus projected coordinate systems, and thematic mapping principles. Produced the first choropleths of Singapore's planning subzones, then went beyond the built-in classification methods to percentile and box maps whose breaks come from the data distribution itself.

Lesson 2 · Spatial point patterns analysis

2 exercises

First-order methods describing where events are dense, and second-order methods describing whether events attract or repel one another and at what distance. The headline result: Singapore's 1,925 childcare centres are strongly clustered, R = 0.552, and the pattern survives every test applied to it.

Lesson 3 · Spatio-temporal point patterns

In progress

Adding time to the point pattern: spatio-temporal kernel density estimation and space-time K-functions, applied to forest fire detections in Kepulauan Bangka Belitung, Indonesia.

Lessons 4 – 10

Ahead

Spatial weights and autocorrelation, emerging hot spot analysis, spatially constrained clustering, geographically weighted models, and spatial interaction and accessibility modelling.

How this site is built

Q

Quarto

Every page is a .qmd document. Code, output and commentary live in one file, so nothing shown here was pasted in by hand. The figures are rendered from the code above them.

R

R 4.5.2

All analysis runs locally and is frozen with freeze: auto, so a published result is reproducible from the exact code beside it.

▲

Vercel

The rendered site is committed and deployed on push, from github.com/imgigi/626.
